body_md:
Kristina Bogic, the 19-year-old star of Netflix's psychological thriller The Body, has discussed the process of landing the role of Anya and developing a character she quickly came to care about. In a November 2026 interview, the actress described her desire to preserve Anya's vulnerability while exploring the more complicated aspects of her personality and choices.

Bogic had only recently turned 18 when the audition arrived. Having experienced rejection through hundreds of previous auditions, she did not initially expect to secure the leading role. Several friends had also auditioned for Anya. Nevertheless, she decided to pursue the opportunity, progressing through callbacks and receiving increasingly substantial portions of the script. Her enthusiasm for the material grew independently of whether she would ultimately be cast.

Anya is the captain of a Catholic high school's dance team. Alongside mysterious incidents affecting the students, she navigates intense social pressures and complicated feelings for her close friend Elise. Bogic sees her as a popular and influential young woman who also possesses a considerable degree of softness and innocence. She believes many young women can recognize aspects of Anya's experience, even when they might disagree with her decisions.

Preparing for the part required more than conventional acting rehearsals. Bogic had not danced for five years and initially felt awkward when asked to submit an improvised dance video. An eight-week training program with choreographer Ryan Heffington helped her regain confidence in her physical movement. She also undertook acting classes and four hours of dialect coaching each week. Becoming comfortable with movement was an important step in discovering how Anya presents herself.

The relationship between Anya and Elise is another central element of the series. Bogic completed four chemistry reads with Sara Boustany, who plays Elise. She recalled that their connection developed naturally from their earliest conversation and that their shared excitement about the project informed their performances. The friendship between the actors continued beyond the immediate demands of filming.

Bogic also praised the supportive atmosphere among the wider cast. Rather than encountering the competition sometimes associated with large groups of young performers, she described an environment in which the actors encouraged one another and developed their characters collaboratively.

For Bogic, playing Anya meant exploring the tension between good intentions, vulnerability and imperfect decisions. The actress's account offers a useful perspective on the character without requiring viewers to know how the season ends. It also highlights the considerable preparation behind a performance that has become part of the online conversation surrounding the Netflix series.
